title: Automated High-Content Multiplex Fluorescence for RNA In Situ Analysis
author: Descarpentrie, Bernard, et al.

steps.title: Perform in situ transcriptomics
steps.instruction: Carry out the chosen in‑situ transcriptomic assay (e.g., RNAscope multiplex V2) on the tissue sections according to the assay’s standard protocol.

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Image the stained sections using a confocal microscope or a tissue‑slide scanner, acquiring 700–1000 high‑quality nuclei per sample; use 40× magnification for digitization (63× optional for confocal, requiring more fields), and avoid epifluorescence microscopy because of its high noise‑to‑signal ratio.

steps.title: Prepare images for Fiji
steps.instruction: Ensure all acquired images are in .TIFF format; if not, convert them with Fiji (download Fiji from https://imagej.net/software/fiji/#downloads for Windows, macOS, or Linux).

steps.title: Separate chromogenic channels (optional)
steps.instruction: For chromogenic in‑situ hybridization, separate colour channels in Fiji before analysis:

substeps.instruction: Open the RGB image in Fiji (Image > Type > RGB).
Choose Image > Color > Color Deconvolution.
Select “From ROI” from the dropdown.
Use the rectangle tool to draw example ROIs for nuclei, probe signal, and background.
Run the deconvolution to generate separate channel images.
Save each channel as a .TIFF file in a new folder for AURA processing.

steps.title: Define segmentation parameters on test image
steps.instruction: Use a single representative image to set AURA segmentation settings:

substeps.instruction: Create a folder containing only the representative .TIFF image.
Start Fiji, click the red double‑arrow in the toolbar, and choose the “AURA light” macro from the dropdown.
When prompted, select the folder created in the previous step (single‑image mode).
In the AURA dialog, set:
– Number of channels (minimum 2, maximum 15) and give each a name without special characters (% $ ! & / \ : ; « » # @).
– Identify which channel contains the nuclear stain.
– Set the maximum expansion area around nuclei (default 0.1 µm; adjust as needed for cell size).
– Choose which channels will be analysed.
– Based on a negative‑control image, set the minimum dot size (default 0.1 µm; set to 0 if no background dots are present).
Click “OK” to run the analysis.
Inspect the generated QC image (found in the same folder); if segmentation is unsatisfactory, repeat the dialog with adjusted parameters.

steps.title: Run batch analysis with AURA
steps.instruction: Process the full image set using the previously defined parameters:

substeps.instruction: Place all .TIFF images to be analysed in a single folder.
In Fiji, click the red double‑arrow and select the “AURA” macro (not the light version).
Select the folder containing the batch of images (AURA can handle batch mode).
In the dialog, repeat the same settings as defined in step 5 (number of channels, channel names, nucleus channel, expansion radius, channels to analyse, minimum dot size).
Click “OK” to start the analysis (≈1 min per 10 images at 40×; longer at higher magnification).
When finished, three sub‑folders will appear inside the image folder:
– Quality_Control (QC images with nuclei in red and dots in yellow).
– Results (one .CSV file per channel per image and an “Analysis_Settings.txt” file).
– ROIs (ROISet .tif files for each image).

steps.title: Inspect output files
steps.instruction: Verify the results generated by AURA:

substeps.instruction: Open the Quality_Control folder and confirm that nuclei are correctly segmented (red overlay) and that dots are correctly detected (yellow overlay) for each channel.
Open the Results folder; each .CSV contains counts per nucleus and the summary .txt file records the parameters used.
To visualise raw ROI data, drag a RoiSet .tif file and its corresponding .TIFF image into Fiji, open the ROI Manager, and select “Show All” and “Labels”.

steps.title: Analyze quantitative results
steps.instruction: Use the spreadsheets produced by AURA to extract biological metrics:

substeps.instruction: Open the detailed quantification spreadsheet (Figure 9A) and the cumulative summary spreadsheet (Figure 9B).
For each channel note:
– Number of cells per bin (0: 0 dots, 1: 1‑3 dots, 2: 4‑9 dots, 3: 10‑15 dots, 4: >15 dots).
– Percentage of positive cells per bin.
– Average dots per cell.
– Number and percentage of double‑ or multiple‑positive (co‑positive) cells.
– H‑score, calculated as Σ(percentage × bin number).
If the analysis was performed with “Area” as the analysis type (step 10b in the original text), use the area‑based values instead of dot counts.
Record the desired metrics for downstream statistical testing.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of data
steps.instruction: Perform appropriate statistical comparisons (e.g., two‑group or multi‑group tests) using Prism 7, GraphPad, or any other statistical software, based on the experimental design.
